text:
maya: :rotating_light: deploy-bot flagged a regression in the new rollout at 14:12 UTC — spikes in p95 latency for /v1/generate. Paging oncall.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] rollout-2024-11-07-ml-v2 -> traffic 10% increased tail latency (>2s p95). Incident ID: INC-1749500000

sam-sre: got it, I'm on pager. looking at dashboard — p95 for 1s gen jumped from 480ms -> 2.4s around 14:11. error rate OK, but queue depth up on gpu-pool-dedicated-3.

jordan-ml: putting initial hypothesis: model v2 uses a new tokenizer variant and q8 kernel that sometimes causes longer KV cache loads for long contexts. canary traffic was 10%.

maya: any customer-facing errors? support reported a couple of slow requests from acme-corp but no 5xx.

eli: i'm taking handoff (15:00 UTC). sam — can you capture timeline + logs and pin down earliest affected shard? I'll pick this up from there.

sam-sre: timeline so far:
- 14:05 deploy started (deploy-bot)
- 14:09 canary->10% traffic
- 14:11 p95 latency jump detected by infra metrics
- 14:12 deploy-bot alert & pager

sam-sre: logs (snip):
```
2024-11-07T14:11:07Z gpu-pool-dedicated-3 req=abc123 model=v2 seq=512 kv_ms=1842 total_ms=2401
2024-11-07T14:11:08Z gpu-pool-dedicated-3 req=abc126 model=v2 seq=1024 kv_ms=1902 total_ms=2603
2024-11-07T14:11:09Z gpu-pool-dedicated-4 req=abc128 model=v1 seq=512 kv_ms=120 total_ms=520
```

sam-sre: note kv_ms on v2 is substantially higher on same seq lengths.

jordan-ml: can you run a quick diff between model v1 and v2 kernel choices? I pushed the compile flags: `--kv-cache-prefetch=true` on v2. If prefetch is regressing on certain CUDA drivers it could stall.

maya: also saw a small uptick in tail open file handles on that pool, maybe I/O backpressure + prefetch.

eli: ok next steps:
- confirm whether only v2 is affected (logs indicate yes)
- run version pin check for any live rollbacks allowed
- check whether autoscaler decisions were impacted

sam-sre: running pin check now:
```
infractl rollout status --name rollout-2024-11-07-ml-v2 --json | jq '.variants[] | {model,traffic,active}'
# result: v1 traffic=90 active=true, v2 traffic=10 active=true
```

sam-sre: rollback window open? commit has autopromote=false, so manual rollback allowed.

ops-bot: @eli you've been assigned incident INC-1749500000. Primary oncall: eli. Escalation: sam-sre.

eli: thanks. Jordan — can you diff the model artifacts (tokenizer, config, compiled kernels)? also dump build id.

jordan-ml: build ids:
- v1: build-20241030-9f2a
- v2: build-20241107-3c7b (kv-prefetch enabled)

jordan-ml: diff (abbreviated):
- tokenizer.vocab: identical
- model.config: relu -> gelu approximation change (shouldn't affect kv)
- compile.flags: +--kv-cache-prefetch +--optimize-kv-async

jordan-ml: possible hypothesis A: kv prefetch + driver anomaly causes stalls when sequence lengths > 512. Hypothesis B: quantization kernels fallback on specific GPU causing much slower execution.

sam-sre: running a targeted canary replay (replay traffic for same requests to v1/v2) — I'll route a 5-minute tape now.

(some minutes pass)

sam-sre: replay results:
- v1 p95 = 470ms
- v2 p95 = 2.3s
- CPU spin and GPU memcpy time increased on v2 nodes. stack trace terse:
```
# profile snippet
nv_copy_async -> wait_event -> memcpy_sync (1800ms)
```

maya: that points to GPU memcpy stalls — matches prefetch hypothesis.

eli: customer impact: looking at routing, canary at 10% affected list of customers = [acme-corp, beta-startup, internal-dev]. CS notified acme-corp of potential slowness 14:25 UTC.

eli: decision time — do we rollback to v1 or patch? We have manual rollback and previous model is healthy. Ops: what are rollback steps & time to safe state?

sam-sre: rollback plan (typical):
1) pin routing to v1: `infractl rollout pin --model v1 --rollout rollout-2024-11-07-ml-v2`
2) scale down v2 instances gracefully
3) monitor p95 & errors for 15m
Estimated safe revert ~ 6 minutes to start, 20 minutes to verify.

eli: i'm going to authorize rollback to minimize customer impact. @jordan-ml and @research please cut a follow-up patch with kv prefetch toggled + more defensive driver checks.

jordan-ml: ack. I'll open PR with config flags + a small perf test harness to validate memcpy paths on affected cuda driver (470.x family).

maya: executing pin now.

maya: `infractl rollout pin --model v1 --rollout rollout-2024-11-07-ml-v2 --reason "rollback due to kv memcpy stalls"`

deploy-bot: Rollout update: v1 -> 100% traffic. v2 scaled to 0. Rolling forward completed at 14:33 UTC.

sam-sre: metrics after rollback (14:38): p95 back to 490ms, queue depth normalized, no increase in 5xx.

eli: good. immediate mitigation worked. Now we need in-incident RCA coordination thread items:
- collect full log dump for 14:00-14:20 from gpu-pool-dedicated-3/4 (sam)
- collect driver versions & node diffs (maya)
- reproduce locally with same driver & memcopy stress (jordan)
- write timeline + annotate with exact build ids and commands (eli)
- customer impact summary & support comms (cs @nina)

sam-sre: uploading logs to shared drive: https://internal.redwood/s/INC-1749500000/logs (snip)

maya: node driver versions:
- gpu-3: nvidia-driver 470.103.01
- gpu-4: nvidia-driver 525.85.05

maya: interesting — v2 scheduled to nodes including gpu-3 (older driver). v1 mostly stayed on newer nodes due to packing differences.

jordan-ml: that could explain why v2 saw memcpy stalls on gpu-3. I'll try setting `--kv-cache-prefetch=false` and forcing run on gpu-3 in staging.

eli: hypothesis tracking in-thread (we'll update states):
- H1: kv-prefetch + older driver -> memcpy stall (High, supported by logs)
- H2: quantization kernel fallback -> slower compute (Medium, need repro)
- H3: increased I/O FD pressure -> indirect backpressure (Low, minor evidence)

sam-sre: marking H1 as primary. collecting repro results now.

(approx 40m later)

jordan-ml: repro successful on node with 470 driver when kv-prefetch enabled: p95 ~ 2.1s. toggling prefetch off yields p95 ~ 480ms. PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ml/merge/2345

eli: great. action items and owners in-thread:
- jordan-ml: PR to disable default prefetch until driver-safe (PR 2345) — in review
- infra: add driver compatibility gate to rollout planner (maya)
- eng-ops: add alert for cross-node driver heterogeneity affecting kernel selection (sam-sre)
- cs/nina: send customer impact note with timeline & apology (nina)

nina: will draft comms. rough customer impact note: "a small portion of canary traffic experienced increased latency between 14:11-14:33 UTC due to a rollout to nodes with older GPU drivers; we've reverted and are testing a fix."

eli: good. tagging this thread for RCA build-out. I'll own final timeline and postmortem. folks, please attach any additional logs and patch links here. closing incident channel in 24h after RCA publish.

ops-bot: Incident INC-1749500000 status: mitigated -> rollback complete. Postmortem owner: eli.

sam-sre: attaching full grep extracts:
```
# grep key traces
grep -E "kv_ms|memcpy|nv_copy_async" /var/logs/gpu-pool-dedicated-3/2024-11-07.log | head -n 50
```

jordan-ml: PR link again: https://git.internal/redwood/ml/merge/2345 (disables kv-prefetch by default, adds driver check)

eli: thanks everyone. final note: we should also update the rollout planner to avoid mixing driver families during staged rollouts. I'll add that as a follow-up in the RCA.
